column2: Drink the soma, Indra; may it delight you, which the stone pressed for you, O bay-horsed, held by the arms of the presser like a horse.
The exhilaration of yours that is lovely, to be yoked, by which you slay Vritras, O bay-horsed — may it delight you, Indra, O lord of wealth.
Hear well this my word, bounteous one, the praise that Vasishtha offers you; accept these prayers at the shared feast.
The sages bow the rim with the eye to the ram in the loud chant; your well-shining, guileless ones, strong, in the ear, with the singers.
The singers have raised their voices together to Indra for the drinking of soma; lord of heaven, when he is strengthened, firm in his vows, with might and helps.
Adorn that Indra, O much-invoked, for help, in whom is the twofold upholding; the thunderbolt is set in his hand, beautiful, great, like a god, like the Sun.
That son, pure, born, made shine his two parents at his birth; great, the two great ones, strengtheners of truth.
Go forth for the dwelling, praised, pleasing to the guileless people; go to the feast for praise.
You indeed, O flowing one, most radiant, proclaim the divine births for immortality.
By which the Navagvas and Dadhyanch uncover the waters, by which the sages obtained kinship; by which they attained the glories in the favor of the gods, the lovely immortal.
With thoughts they cleanse the racer playing in the wood on the sheep's wool; the prayers sang together to the three-backed one.
The showering one has been released toward the vessels like a swift horse seeking strength; purifying, he gives birth to speech, he runs.
The Brahman of the gods, the leader of the seers, the sage of the wise, the buffalo of the beasts, the falcon of the vultures, the axe of the woods — Soma crosses the filter roaring.
The river waves the wave of speech, songs and thoughts as it flows; seeing within, the bull stands in the lower realms among the cows, knowing.
May this one be with us as Tvashtar is among forms to be fashioned, by the skill of this famed one.
This Agni goes over all glories, rules among the gods; may he come to us with strengths.
None is a better charioteer than you, Indra, when you drive your two bay horses; none attains your might; none has good horses like you.
Now honor Indra and speak hymns; the pressed drops have rejoiced; bow to the eldest strength.
Enjoy, Indra, come forth, bay-horsed hero; drink the pressed soma like a thought; loving honey, lovely, for exhilaration.
Fill your new belly with honey, Indra, as heaven with water; by the sound of this pressed soma the fair-spoken exhilarations have stood near you.
Indra, the swift conqueror, like Mitra, slew Vritra; like an ascetic he split Vala; like Bhrigu he overcame foes in the joy of soma.
Finder of cattle, flow, finder of wealth, finder of gold, O drop, seed-bearer, placed in the worlds; you, Soma, are well-heroic, all-knowing; men sit near you with songs.
You are the all-seeing watcher of men, Soma; flowing, O bull, you run apart; flow for us with wealth and gold; may we live in the worlds.
Ruling, you go through these worlds, O drop, with your fair-winged bay mares yoked; let them stream honey, ghee and milk for you; in your law, Soma, let the peoples abide.
The courses of you, flowing all-knowing one, have been released like the rays of the sun.
Making a banner above heaven, you move toward all forms; you swell, Soma, like an ocean.
Born, you drive speech to the rite, flowing, roaring like the god Sun.
The somas have run forth, the flowing drops, mingling in the waters, they cleanse.
The cows ran toward them like waters flowing down; purified, they reached Indra.
Flow forth, flowing Soma, exhilarating for Indra; held by men, you are led apart.
O drop, when pressed by stones you are surrounded by the filter; enough for the abode of Indra.
You, Soma, men's delight, flow, upholder of peoples, victor, to be rejoiced in.
Flow, best Vritra-slayer, to be gladdened by hymns, pure, purifying, wonderful.
The pure, purifying one is called Soma, pressed, honeyed, guardian of the gods, slayer of the evil-speaking.
The seer is cleansed for the gods' feast through the woolen sieves, overcoming all rivals.
He indeed sends to the singers strength rich in cattle, a thousandfold, flowing.
You are cleansed by the mind, all-around, and you flow by thought; may you, Soma, find us fame.
Flow great fame and firm wealth to the bounteous; bring food to the singers.
Like a king of good vows you have entered the songs, Soma, purifying, O wonderful carrier.
That carrier in the waters, hard to cross, cleansed by the hands, Soma sits in the vessels.
Like a playing sacrifice-giver, loving greatness, you go to the filter, Soma, giving heroic strength to the praiser.
Grain by grain, fatten us with the drink; flow around, Soma, with all good fortune.
O drop, as is your praise, as is your birth of the drink, sit in the dear grass.
And for us, finder of cattle and horses, flow, Soma, with drink — swiftest in these days.
He who conquers and is not conquered, who strikes the foe by approaching — flow as the winner of thousands.
By those honey-dripping streams of yours, O drop, that have been released for help — by them you sit on the filter.
Flow to Indra for drinking across the woolen sieves, sitting in the womb of truth.
You, Soma, flow around, sweetest for the Angirases, the finder of room, ghee and milk.
Your glories, O Agni, are noticed like the rain's lightning, like the courses of the dawns; when you are sent among the plants and woods, you yourself gather food in your mouth.
Urged by the wind, sped, when you stand devouring the thirsty food after your desire — your streams strive like chariots separately, O ageless Agni, burning.
The wisdom-maker, accomplisher of the rite, Agni the priest, the overcomer of thought; to you the great ones choose the like of a small offering, none other than you.
Indeed, Varuna, your help is great, now; Mitra, I desire your favor.
May we reach with right guileless thoughts your two abode; may we be yours, Mitras.
Protect us, Mitras, with your guardians, and save us, O good saviors; may we overcome the Dasyus with our bodies.
Rising with might, having drunk, you shook the two jaws; the soma pressed in the vessels, Indra.
Both heaven and earth rejoiced after you as you contended, Indra, when you became slayer of the Dasyu.
I hold speech with eight feet, with nine bonds, the strengthener of truth; I measured the body from Indra.
Indra and Agni, these hymns have sung to you; drink the pressed soma, bringers of joy.
By those much-desired teams of yours, O men, for the giver, come, Indra and Agni.
Come by those, O men, to this pressed libation, Indra and Agni, to drink the soma.
The waters have flowed for Indra, Vayu, Varuna, the Maruts, may the somas flow to Vishnu.
Granting food to our offspring, Soma, from all sides flow to us a thousandfold.
In the water-meadow, rich in cattle, you flowed with cows; Soma flowed with the milked ones; like coverings they came into the sea; joyful, he flows for exhilaration.
Whatever wondrous, praiseworthy, heavenly or earthly wealth, Soma — purifying, bring us that.
The bull, purifying the lives, thundering on the grass, the bay one sat in his own nest.
You two are lords of heaven, Indra and Soma, lords of cattle; ruling, nourish our thoughts.
You are a hero, to be armed; you take much away; you strengthen even the small one; you teach the pressing sacrificer, much is your wealth.
When contests arise, wealth is set for the bold; yoke your two bay horses that drop exhilaration; whom do you slay, in whose wealth do you place us, Indra?
The fair-skinned ones drink of the sweet, all-spread honey, who with Indra, the bull, are joyful for beauty, wealthy, according to self-rule.
They, the dappled ones, desiring the dappled, mingle his soma; the dear cows of Indra urge on the thunderbolt, the arrow, according to self-rule.
With homage the wise attend to his strength; they have followed his many vows for the first knowledge, according to self-rule.
The bright drink, wind-borne by the gods, washed in the waters, pressed by men; the cows sweeten it with milk.
Then they adorned him like a horse for the urger, for immortality, the essence of honey in the shared feast.
O lord of food, shine great splendor and fame, O god, the god-seeking; open the middle vessel, young one.
Be spoken of, O skilful one, pressed in the vessels, carrier of the clans, like a lord of the people; send the rain of heaven, urging the flow of waters, for the seeking of cattle through thought.
Near the two drinking-places of Trita, he shared the hidden step of the sacrifice, with seven abodes, dear.
With the stream of Trita he sent three kinds of wealth upon the backs; the skilful one measures out his courses.
Flow for the winning of strength, pressed in the filter with the stream; for Indra, Soma, for Vishnu, for the gods, the most honeyed.
The thoughts lick you, the bay one, the guileless in the filter, as mothers lick the newborn calf, O flowing one, in the rite.
You, great-vowed, have sustained both heaven and earth; you freed the bound garment, flowing, by your greatness.
Then, mixed with the honeyed stream, the stone-milked one flows through the wool; the drop, enjoying Indra's friendship, a god, the exhilaration of the god, for exhilaration.
Purifying, the god flows toward the rites, mingling with the gods by his own essence; the drop, clad in the laws in their seasons, the ten fingers, in the sheep's wool on the peak.
To you, Agni, with the verse comes the offering, O lord of the bright light, O fair-shining, wonderful lord of the people; the offering-carrier is invoked for you; bring food to the singers.
O fair-shining lord of the people, you fill both ladles at the mouth; and also fill us in the hymns, O lord of strength; bring food to the singers.
Sing the great Saman to Indra, the wise, the great, the prayer-maker, the sage, the wonder-worker.
You, Indra, are the overcomer; you made the sun shine; you are Vishvakarman, all-divine, great.
You went with light to the shining realm of heaven; the gods held back for your friendship, Indra.
Mount your chariot, Vritra-slayer; your two bay horses are yoked by prayer; let the pressing-stone with its sound make your mind turn toward us.
The two bay horses carry Indra, of unassailable strength, to the good praises of the sages and the sacrifice of men.
The light of the sacrifice flows, the dear honey; the father of the gods, the begetter, the all-pervasive wealth; he sets the jewel of the two worlds, the most exhilarating, joyful, powerful essence.
Roaring, the racer runs to the vessel, lord of heaven, hundred-streamed, all-seeing; the bay one sits in the dwellings of Mitra, cleansed by the sheep's wool and rivers, the bull.
Flowing, you run in front of the rivers; you go first of speech among the cows; in front you take a great prize of strength; well-armed, Soma, you are pressed by the pressers.
Adorned by the truth-lovers, cleansed by the hands, those somas bring the giver all the divine and earthly wealth; let those of the air flow.
Flow, god-protector, across the filter quickly, Soma; O drop, the bull, enter Indra.
Be spoken of, great delight, bull, drop, most splendid; sit, sustainer, in the nest.
The streams of the pressed sage have milked the dear honey; the skilful one has clothed the waters.
The great waters, the rivers, flow after you, the great, when you are clothed with cows.
The ocean in the waters is cleansed, the prop, the support of heaven; Soma in the filter longs for us.
Your songs, O drop, adorn you with might, the working ones, with which you are decorated for exhilaration.
We ask that you, the bold world-maker, for exhilaration, for your great praise.
